themes_detail.label: Tree Damage & Dead Trees Surge
themes_detail.summary: Astoria/LIC experiencing a sharp spike in complaints about illegal tree damage (9 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average) and dead/dying trees (8 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average)—a combined 454-433% increase—suggesting possible storm damage, construction impact, or neglected maintenance affecting the district's urban canopy.
evidence: Illegal Tree Damage: 9 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average (z-score: 7.43, +454%)
Dead/Dying Tree: 8 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 5.31, +433%)
Combined signal suggests acute environmental stressor affecting neighborhood in past 7 days
reporting_angles: Did a recent storm or weather event trigger the spike? Cross-reference with NWS data.
Is new construction (705 DOB permits filed in last 90 days, including 42 demolitions) damaging nearby street trees?

themes_detail.label: Water Quality Emergency Signal
themes_detail.summary: Water Quality complaints spiked to 7 complaints 2 weeks ago from 0.4 weekly average—a staggering 1767% increase (z-score: 13.68)—the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset, indicating potential contamination, pipe breaks, or supply issues affecting potability or appearance in the district.
evidence: Water Quality: 7 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 13.68, +1767%) — highest z-score in dataset
Timing suggests spike began roughly 2 weeks ago; unclear if still ongoing
No recent local news coverage or community board discussion documented—possible coverage gap
reporting_angles: Contact DEP for emergency water quality reports, boil water advisories, or main breaks in CD 401 from 2 weeks ago to present
Interview affected residents: discoloration, odor, taste issues; check social media for corroboration
Cross-reference with HEAT/HOT WATER spike (1824 complaints, baseline high) to see if related to infrastructure failure

themes_detail.label: Food Service Regulation Surge
themes_detail.summary: Food Establishment complaints jumped to 19 last week from 7 weekly average (+171%, z-score: 5.24), while Outdoor Dining complaints spiked to 7 last week from 0.8 average (+833%, z-score: 6.45)—signaling possible health/safety violations, overcrowding, or enforcement focus on restaurants and sidewalk dining in LIC/Astoria.
evidence: Food Establishment: 19 complaints last week vs. 7.0 weekly average (z-score: 5.24, +171%)
Outdoor Dining: 7 complaints last week vs. 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 6.45, +833%)
Combined signal points to restaurant/dining venue issues; coincides with post-holiday dining surge
reporting_angles: Request DOHMH inspection data for CD 401 (last week): violations, permits, closures
Are outdoor dining sidewalk sheds improperly placed or abandoned post-pandemic removal deadline?
Interview small restaurant owners: are new regulations, rent pressures, or food costs driving complaints?

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street Sign - Damaged complaints spiked to 7 last week from 1.6 weekly average (+331%, z-score: 6.27), while Street Condition remains high baseline (1387 complaints over 90 days), suggesting systemic street maintenance backlog or recent vandalism/weather damage affecting navigation and safety.
evidence: Street Sign - Damaged: 7 complaints last week vs. 1.6 weekly average (z-score: 6.27, +331%)
Street Condition: 1387 complaints over 90-day period—baseline high concern
Spikes suggest acute damage event; street condition baseline suggests chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Did recent winter weather (snow/ice at 1486 complaints) or heavy winds topple or damage signage?
Request DOT maintenance records: when were street signs last inspected/replaced in CD 401?
Link to CB budget requests: has the district repeatedly asked for street maintenance funding that remains unfunded?
